help.gm_journey_desc: Each stage reaches 40 years further back in time and gives you less time per round. Hit the stage's accuracy gate to unlock the next one — retry as often as you like.
help.gm_journey_features: 100 stages|Accuracy gate|5–10 rounds per stage|5 min → 30 s per round|Unlimited retries
help.gm_practice_desc: Play as many 5-round games as you like. Pick the eras and regions you want and set a round timer from 15 s to 5 min, or turn it off.
help.gm_challenge_desc: Create a lobby, invite players or share the join link, then choose Live or Anytime. The host sets the timer, year range and deadline.
help.gm_challenge_features: 5 rounds|Live: up to 8 players|Anytime: up to 30 players|Invites & share link
help.sc_intro: Every round is scored on two axes, each from 0 to 100%: WHERE (how close your pin is) and WHEN (how close your year is).
help.sc_where_desc: An exact hit scores 100%. Accuracy then falls smoothly with distance, so the first few hundred kilometres matter most.
help.sc_when_desc: Based on how many years off you are. Older events are more forgiving: the further back an event is, the less the same miss costs.
help.sc_xp_desc: Round XP = WHERE accuracy + WHEN accuracy, after hint costs. A perfect round earns 200 XP, so a 5-round game is worth up to 1,000 XP. Your round accuracy is the average of the two.
help.sc_missing: No pin or no year when the round ends? That axis scores 0.
help.hints_intro: Open Hints during a round to see 5 WHEN and 5 WHERE hints. Tap any hint to reveal it instantly — there is no confirmation and no required order.
help.hints_cost: Each hint shows its cost: a percentage taken off that axis's accuracy for the round. Costs on the same axis add up (capped at 100%), and WHEN costs are reduced for older events.
help.hints_xp: Because XP is the sum of both accuracies, every hint also lowers your XP.
help.badges_intro: After every round you can earn a badge for WHERE, WHEN and Combo accuracy. Combo uses the lower of your two scores, so it rewards rounds that are strong on both.
help.badges_near_miss: Near-miss (88–89%): shown when you just miss Bronze.
help.badges_after_hints: Badges use your accuracy after hint costs.
help.acc_account_desc: Change your username, see your email and member-since date, adjust settings and sign out.
help.acc_settings_desc: Turn sound and vibration on or off, and choose kilometres or miles for distances.
help.acc_avatar_desc: Pick a historical figure as your avatar when you sign up, and change it any time from your Profile.
help.acc_notif_desc: On the Account page, choose how you receive game invitations and "a player finished a game" alerts: push, in-app, both or none. Tap the bell in the top bar to see recent notifications.
help.faq_a1: Each round scores WHERE (distance from the real location) and WHEN (years off) from 0 to 100%. Your round XP is the sum of both — up to 200 per round. Hints lower the accuracy of the axis they belong to. See Scoring & XP for examples.
help.faq_q2: Do I need an account to play?
help.faq_a2: Yes. Sign up for free with email or Google to play, save your stats and XP, appear in rankings and play with friends.
help.faq_a3: Daily (the same 5 events for everyone, one attempt per day), Your Journey (100 stages with an accuracy gate), Practice (unlimited solo games with your own filters) and Challenge (play with friends, Live or Anytime).
help.faq_a4: Open Hints during a round. There are 5 WHEN and 5 WHERE hints; tap one to reveal it instantly. Each costs a percentage of that axis's accuracy (shown on the hint), and costs on the same axis add up.
help.faq_q5: What is the difference between Live and Anytime?
help.faq_a5: Live: everyone plays the same round at the same time (up to 8 players), with an optional round timer and shared results between rounds. Anytime: each player plays the 5 rounds at their own pace before the deadline set by the host (1–14 days), up to 30 players.
help.faq_q6: Can I zoom into the photo?
help.faq_a6: Yes. Pinch to zoom on mobile or use the mouse wheel on desktop, drag to pan, and double-click to toggle zoom. On the results screen you can also open the photo full screen.
help.faq_q7: What happens when the timer runs out?
help.faq_a7: Whatever you have set — pin, year or both — is submitted automatically. Anything you didn't set scores 0 on that axis. In Anytime games only your own round is affected.
help.faq_a8: A new Daily starts every day at 10:00 UTC (midnight in UTC+14, the first time zone to reach the new day). The home page shows a countdown. You get one attempt per Daily, and an unfinished attempt can be resumed.
help.faq_a9: Each stage shows its pass mark. Finish the stage with an accuracy at or above it to unlock the next stage. Retry as often as you like — later stages cover a wider span of history with less time per round.
help.faq_a10: Score 90% or more on WHERE, WHEN or Combo in a round: Bronze from 90%, Silver from 95% and Gold at 100%. See Badges for details.
help.ts_t1_problem: The game doesn't load or shows a black screen
help.ts_t1_solution: Refresh the page. If it persists, clear this site's cache and cookies and reload in an up-to-date Chrome, Firefox, Safari or Edge.
help.ts_t2_problem: My friend didn't receive the invite
help.ts_t2_solution: Invites appear in the bell in the top bar and under Invitations on the home page. Make sure your friend is signed in, or send them the share link from the lobby.
help.ts_t3_problem: The timer ran out before I could submit
help.ts_t3_solution: Guesses are submitted automatically when time is up. In Challenge the host can set a longer round timer or turn it off, and in Practice you choose your own timer. Daily (90 s) and Journey timers are fixed.
help.ts_t4_solution: A hint's content appears only after you tap it. Hints you've already revealed show a check mark and stay visible for the rest of the round.
help.ts_t5_problem: My score is lower than expected
help.ts_t5_solution: Check the hints you used — each one lowers that axis's accuracy. Location accuracy also drops quickly with distance, and a missing pin or year scores 0 on that axis.
help.ts_t6_solution: Choose Push or Both in the Notifications settings on the Account page and allow notifications in your browser. On iPhone, push only works after adding Guess-History to your Home Screen.

lobby.help_game_settings:
Choose how this Compete session plays out.

ANYTIME (Own Pace) — Asynchronous. Each player plays all 5 rounds independently, at their own speed — no waiting on anyone else. The session stays open for the deadline you set below (1–14 days). You can optionally turn on a per-round timer; if a player runs out of time on a round, only that round auto-submits for them — nobody else is affected.

LIVE (Live Challenge) — Synchronous. Everyone plays the same round at the same time. Each round has an optional countdown timer (15 seconds to 5 minutes). After everyone submits, results are shown to all players together, with an auto-advance timer to the next round.

Round Timer — Optional. How long each player has to submit a guess for a round.
Results Timer — The maximum time available to view the round results before automatically advancing to the next round.
Game Timer (Anytime only) — The overall deadline for the whole session, from 1 to 14 days after you start the game.

Players you invite will appear in the lobby once they accept. As host, you can remove a player from the lobby at any time before the game starts.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Guess-History ("we," "us," "our") operates the website www.guess-history.com (the "Service"), a multiplayer historical geography and year-guessing game. This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect, how we use it, and your rights regarding that information.
privacy.account_info_text: When you sign in via Google or email/password, we receive your email address, display name, and profile picture (if provided by Google). Authentication is handled by Supabase.
privacy.gameplay_data_text: We store your game sessions, guesses (year and location), scores, accuracy statistics, badges, and leaderboard rankings to operate the Service and show you your history and progress.
privacy.usage_data_text: We may automatically collect standard technical data such as IP address, browser type, device type, and pages visited, for security, debugging, and service reliability purposes.
privacy.images_text: Historical event images used in gameplay are served from our own image infrastructure (Firebase Storage). We do not use your personal photos.
privacy.use_provide: Provide, operate, and maintain the Service (game sessions, multiplayer matchmaking, leaderboards)

privacy.use_track: Track your scores, stats, badges, and progress across game modes
privacy.use_improve: Diagnose bugs and improve performance and reliability
privacy.use_communicate: Communicate with you about your account or the Service, if necessary
privacy.no_sell: We do not sell your personal information. We do not use your data for third-party advertising.
privacy.providers_intro: We use the following third-party service providers to operate Guess-History:
privacy.providers_outro: Each provider processes data only as necessary to provide their respective service to us and is bound by their own privacy and security practices.
privacy.cookies_text: We use cookies and browser local storage to maintain your login session and game state (e.g., resuming an in-progress round after a page refresh). These are functional, not advertising, cookies.
privacy.retention_text: We retain account and gameplay data for as long as your account is active. You may request deletion of your account and associated data at any time by contacting us (see Section 8).
privacy.security_text: We take reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect your information, including encrypted connections (HTTPS) and access-controlled databases. No method of transmission or storage is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.
privacy.children_text: The Service is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13.
privacy.contact_text: For privacy questions, data deletion requests, or other concerns, contact us at: appymanya@gmail.com
privacy.changes_text: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Material changes will be reflected by an updated "Last updated" date on this page.

grow_deck.meta_description: A cinematic investor presentation: from a history game to a human-grounded visual AI benchmark.
grow_deck.title: Guess History

s01.headline: Every round of this game makes an AI benchmark harder to fake.
body: Guess History is a game: a historical scene appears, and players say where and when it happened.
Every answer is recorded. Together they become a human baseline for how well machines understand history.
statements: The game is the distribution. The benchmark is the product.
s01.alt: Cinematic historical scene with depth, human figures, and visually ambiguous clues

s02.headline: Two questions. No instructions.
body: A scene appears. Players mark the place on a map and set the year on a slider. The reveal shows the truth and the distance from it.
s02.alt: Historical scene used for the where-and-when mini-demo

s03.headline: Players aren't just playing.
body: Each round produces a place guess, a year guess and a confidence. Aggregated per image, that becomes measured difficulty instead of curated difficulty.
s03.final: The benchmark is a by-product of play.
s03.alt: The same historical image used to anchor the accumulating human observations

s04.headline: Then ask the same questions of a model.
body: Same image, same two questions, same scoring. A human baseline only matters if a model can be measured against it.
s04.final: Same image. Same questions. Comparable answers.
s04.alt: Split-screen visual showing the same image tested against a human and an AI model

s05.headline: The report is the product.
body: Not a leaderboard position: a breakdown of how a model reasons about time, space and its own certainty.
s05.final: Right or wrong is the least interesting output.
s05.baseline: Human baseline on the same scenes: 8 yr · 74 km

s06.headline: The image is not the asset.
body: Anyone can license a photograph. What compounds is the record around it: who answered, how confidently, how wrong, and which model version was measured against it.
s06.final: The dataset around the image is the moat.
s06.alt: Historical image with progressively denser data layers building around it

s07.headline: Test a model in one run.
body: A provider submits a vision model. The benchmark runs the same scenes through the same scoring code and returns a report anyone can reproduce from the dataset version.

s08.headline: Don't test a model once.
body: A single score is a snapshot. The recurring product is the line: the same benchmark re-run on every release, so a regression is visible the day it ships.

s09.headline: Four ways the benchmark becomes revenue.
body: Evaluation is sold as access, not as a score: automated runs, continuous monitoring, custom programs and controlled data licensing.

s10.headline: The game feeds the benchmark. The benchmark funds the game.
body: Consumer play produces the data. B2B evaluation pays for it. Neither side works without the other.

s11.headline: History is the first domain, not the only one.
body: The method is portable: real scenes, two questions, a human baseline. Anywhere ground truth exists, the same benchmark can be rebuilt.
s11.final: Human-grounded visual evaluation, domain by domain.

s12.headline: Two businesses, one engine.

businesses.title: GUESS HISTORY
businesses.description: A game that attracts players and produces proprietary human annotation.

businesses.title: GUESS HISTORY EVALUATION
businesses.description: A platform that measures AI performance against that annotation.

s12.final: Can AI understand history as well as humans?
